data.title: GEOPOLITICS | Russia’s Vostok Oil Ships First Crude on Arctic Tanker
data.description:
Russia’s giant Vostok Oil project in the Taimyr region has loaded its first crude for shipment via the Northern Sea Route, according to Bloomberg.

The move expands Russia’s presence in the Arctic and opens the way for future growth in oil production.

data.title: Trump Administration Pressures Fed To Avoid Rate Hike Ahead Of September Meeting
data.description: According to CNBC, President Donald Trump and senior administration officials have mounted a public campaign to stop the Federal Reserve from raising interest rates at its Sept. 15-16 meeting, with Trump threatening to halt trade with countries that run surpluses with the U.S. unless the Fed cuts rates. Vice President JD Vance said the Fed should be lowering rates, while Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in a CNBC interview that the central bank typically does not raise rates during a supply shock until second- or third-order inflation effects emerge. Markets are pricing in about a 60% probability of a rate hike, helped by a strong jobs report Friday, and the administration has pointed to a three-month annualized core CPI rate of 1.6% versus just over 3% for the three-month annualized core PCE price index. Fed officials have said the Friday CPI report will be a key gauge of whether inflation is easing or still accelerating.

data.title: Jim Cramer Trims Broadcom, Palo Alto Networks, Adds BNY, Kimberly-Clark and Micron
data.description:
According to CNBC, Jim Cramer’s portfolio reduced exposure to some artificial intelligence winners last week, including trimming Palo Alto Networks ahead of earnings and exiting Corning, while adding BNY, Kimberly-Clark and Micron. The moves came as the S&P 500 rose 0.1% for the week and the Nasdaq gained 0.4%, with both indexes posting their fifth weekly advance in six weeks.

Broadcom remained under pressure despite better-than-expected revenue and earnings. CEO Hock Tan raised his fiscal 2027 AI revenue forecast to $115 billion and said it is expected to double to $230 billion in fiscal 2028. Cramer also said he sold half of the remaining Broadcom position before earnings and is willing to keep the rest because of the company’s relationship with AI startup Anthropic.

Palo Alto Networks reported strong results after Tuesday’s close, and Cramer said AI remains a major tailwind for cybersecurity. He said roughly $1 trillion of global cybersecurity infrastructure needs to be modernized and noted that the stock fell more than 10% last week after profit-taking. Nvidia also rose 6% last week after its $12.9 billion acquisition of Hugging Face, which Cramer said deepens the ecosystem around its chips and gives it access to an open-source AI platform used by more than 18 million developers.
